description: Figure 5 presents a line plot illustrating the Mean Reciprocal Rank at 10 (MRR@10) performance of the Dense Passage Retrieval (DPR) model under four different expansion strategies as the number of queries used during inference increases from 1 to 10. The x-axis, labeled “Number of queries used during inference (S),” is linearly scaled from 1 to 10, with tick marks at integer intervals. The y-axis, labeled “MRR@10,” is linearly scaled from 33.0 to 36.0, with tick marks at 0.5 intervals. Four distinct lines represent the different expansion methods: a black solid line for “DPR w/o query,” a red dashed line for “DPR w/ corpus expansion,” a green dashed line for “DPR w/ document expansion,” and a blue dashed line for “DPR w/ asymmetric expansion.” The “DPR w/o query” line starts at approximately 34.5 and remains relatively flat, showing a slight decline to about 34.4 by S=10. The “DPR w/ corpus expansion” line begins at approximately 35.0, rises to a peak of 35.7 at S=2, then plateaus near 35.6 for S=3 to 10. The “DPR w/ document expansion” line starts at approximately 34.8, rises to a peak of 35.2 at S=2, then declines to about 34.6 by S=10. The “DPR w/ asymmetric expansion” line begins at approximately 34.8, rises to a peak of 35.1 at S=2, then declines to about 34.4 by S=10.
